Its men recovered the bodies of Saul and his sons from Beth-shan and buried them (1 Samuel 31).
David blessed the men of Jabesh-gilead for burying Saul (2 Samuel 2).
David later moved the bones of Saul and Jonathan from Jabesh-gilead to their family tomb (2 Samuel 21).

name: Jabesh
what: Short name for Jabesh-gilead, a town in Gilead east of the Jordan.
today: Possibly Tell el-Maqlub on Wadi Yabis in northern Jordan.
key: The men of Jabesh asked for terms when Nahash besieged them, and Saul rescued them (1 Samuel 11).
The valiant men of Jabesh buried the bones of Saul and his sons (1 Samuel 31).
They fasted seven days after burying Saul under the tree in Jabesh (1 Chronicles 10).

name: Dothan
what: A town in the hill country north of Samaria, beside a route used by traveling caravans.
today: Tell Dothan, south of Jenin, West Bank.
key: Joseph found his brothers pasturing flocks at Dothan, where they threw him into a pit (Genesis 37).
The brothers sold Joseph to Ishmaelite traders passing by on their way to Egypt (Genesis 37).
At Dothan, God opened Elisha's servant's eyes to see horses and chariots of fire (2 Kings 6).
God struck the Syrian army with blindness, and Elisha led them to Samaria (2 Kings 6).

name: Ibleam
what: A Canaanite town in the northern hill country, allotted to Manasseh.
today: Khirbet Bel'ameh, just south of Jenin.
key: Ibleam was assigned to Manasseh, though it lay within Issachar and Asher (Joshua 17).
Manasseh failed to drive out the Canaanites living in Ibleam (Judges 1).
Jehu's men wounded King Ahaziah at the ascent of Gur, near Ibleam (2 Kings 9).

name: Gath-rimmon
what: A Levitical town listed from the western half-tribe of Manasseh, distinct from Dan's Gath-rimmon.
today: Exact site unknown; possibly Ibleam, near Jenin, West Bank.
key: Gath-rimmon, with Taanach, was given from the half-tribe of Manasseh to the Kohathite Levites (Joshua 21).
The parallel list of Levitical towns names Aner and Bileam from Manasseh instead (1 Chronicles 6).

name: Gur
what: An ascent near Ibleam in the northern hill country, where Jehu's men wounded King Ahaziah.
today: Exact site unknown; near Ibleam, south of Jenin, West Bank.
key: Jehu's men shot King Ahaziah of Judah at the ascent of Gur, near Ibleam (2 Kings 9).
Ahaziah fled to Megiddo and died there, and his servants carried him to Jerusalem (2 Kings 9).

name: Bileam
what: A Levitical town of western Manasseh given to Kohathite clans, probably the same town as Ibleam.
today: Likely Khirbet Bel'ameh, just south of Jenin.
key: From the half-tribe of Manasseh, Bileam with its pasturelands went to the rest of the Kohathite clans (1 Chronicles 6).
Joshua's parallel list names Gath-rimmon with Taanach from the half-tribe of Manasseh (Joshua 21).

name: West Manasseh
what: The territory of the half-tribe of Manasseh west of the Jordan, north of Ephraim.
today: Northern West Bank and north-central Israel
key: Moses blessed Joseph's tribes, including the thousands of Manasseh (Deuteronomy 33).
Manasseh received land west of the Jordan, including for Zelophehad's daughters (Joshua 17).
Manasseh failed to drive out the Canaanites from Beth-shean and other towns (Judges 1).
Ezekiel's vision gives Manasseh a portion in the restored land (Ezekiel 48).

name: Salecah
what: A city on the eastern edge of Bashan, marking the limit of Og's kingdom.
today: Likely Salkhad, in southern Syria.
key: Israel takes the cities of Og's kingdom as far as Salecah (Deuteronomy 3).
Og king of Bashan ruled as far as Salecah (Joshua 12).
Salecah marks the eastern limit of the land given east of the Jordan (Joshua 13).
The Gadites live in Bashan as far as Salecah (1 Chronicles 5).

name: Caesarea
what: A Roman port city on the Mediterranean, the seat of the Roman governors of Judea.
today: Caesarea, on the coast of Israel
key: Philip preached in all the towns until he came to Caesarea (Acts 8).
Peter preached to the centurion Cornelius in Caesarea, and Gentiles received the Spirit (Acts 10).
Herod Agrippa was struck down by an angel at Caesarea (Acts 12).
Paul stayed with Philip the evangelist in Caesarea (Acts 21).
Paul was held in Caesarea and appealed to Caesar before Festus (Acts 25).

name: Beth-shean
what: A strong Canaanite city where the Jezreel Valley meets the Jordan Valley.
today: Tel Beit She'an, in northern Israel.
key: The Canaanites of Beth-shean had chariots of iron (Joshua 17).
Manasseh did not drive out the inhabitants of Beth-shean (Judges 1).
Beth-shean was in one of Solomon's administrative districts (1 Kings 4).
It is listed among the towns of Manasseh's descendants (1 Chronicles 7).

name: Beth-shan
what: A fortified city at the junction of the Jezreel and Jordan valleys.
today: Tel Beit She'an, beside the modern town of Beit She'an, Israel.
key: The Philistines fastened the bodies of Saul and his sons to the wall of Beth-shan (1 Samuel 31).
Men of Jabesh-gilead traveled by night to take the bodies down and bury them (1 Samuel 31).
David later recovered the bones of Saul and Jonathan, taken from Beth-shan's square (2 Samuel 21).
